title: The gate ladder: affected checks per task, the full gate and tree scanners per phase, CI under eight minutes
description: The same full set of checks runs per task, per phase, locally and in CI several times, and the set is large because the product carries its own tree lints as tests. Measured: a task gate in the dogfood plan took 716 s, of which the sweep was 384 s and the panel browser gate 282 s; a narrow task gate measured 1,327 s because derived affected steps re-ran 506 s of suites its own full-sweep key had already run; the sweep is 6 min 36 s of wall and 34.6 min of CPU, and CI runs take 12 to 15 minutes. The CI half of this ladder (one executable gate description, skip of a green SHA, the codec cells) is already the earlier F1 phase's; this phase adds the per-task and per-phase rungs and the remaining speed.
desiredOutcome: A task's gate is the selection of checks its change affects, trusted only after its miss rate was measured on this repository's history; tree scanners and the full gate, browser steps included, run once per phase and on push, never per task; a probe of the guarded lints runs at sign-off only when the phase changed them; the sweep's wall clock is under four minutes and CI is under eight minutes and 55 runner-minutes, each measured with the same command before and after; one commit verb writes the index and the shard together, so adding a task mid-phase never leaves the plan uncommittable; and red-first through a sweep-shaped command proves when the task's suites pass.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: acceptance (5) 'the measured result over 20 commits is recorded in the task outcome with the commit range'. The outcome records a 2-commit window (ad586f07b..d33730d60) in which one commit timed out at 1200s (NOT MEASURED) and the other was a full-set selection ('so no suite can be missed'), giving 'misses 0 of 1 commits (mutation); 0 of 1 runs (CI)'. That is zero evidence about the miss rate and not the 20-commit measurement the clause asks for; the executor itself says the 20-commit run is 'still owed by the orchestrator'. The 'misses 0 of 1' line must not be read as a clean miss rate.
findings.resolution: Run the 20-commit command the outcome names on a quiet machine (python3 tools/measure-affected-miss.py --commits 20 --budget-minutes 240 --timeout 2400 --ci-limit 30 --json) and record its output and commit range in the outcome before the task closes done; or, if the orchestrator decides the measurement is out of scope for this task, split it into its own task rather than close this one as met. If the task is closed with no change (--no-change --reason), the reason must say acceptance (5) is unmeasured.

findings.issue: P142.3's description is a verbatim re-ask of a task already done (b52ba79a, amended 66b3635d): tools/measure-affected-miss.py has existed since P131.16-dau, so this task adds nothing and its tests.add entries are met only by pre-existing cases m6, m8, m10, m13. A duplicate task in the plan is an input error that wastes an executor run and can double-count 'tests added'.
findings.resolution: Close P142.3 with --no-change and a reason naming b52ba79a/66b3635d and the pre-existing cases, after (5) is measured; or rewrite its description to the measurement alone.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "a phase touching no such file runs none and says so" / acceptance (2) "prints that it ran none" on the held path: a run that printed `ran none` is held as `state["lintProbe"] = {"head": head}` (the word is not stored), and the held branch then appends `lint probe green (held at this HEAD)` - so any re-entry at the same HEAD (e.g. after the sign-off verb stopped) reports a probe that ran no row as green, the exact reading-as-a-proof the clause forbids.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): Store the word with the hold (`{"head": head, "said": "ran none"|"green"}`) and echo it on the held branch (`lint probe ran none (held at this HEAD)`); add an lp6 twin that holds a ran-none run and asserts the held did-line says ran none.

findings.issue: The success print breaks the module's stated invariant `INSTRUCTION_BYTES = 300` ("The bound every print that is not a stop stays inside") whenever a probe runs: the executor's own measurement is 312 bytes in lp1's one-task fixture. This repo keeps tools/prove-gates.py, so from this change every sign-off here prints past the bound; lp1 does not assert the bound and dp3 only measures a probeless fixture, so nothing goes red.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): Make the probe clause fit (e.g. fold it into the `invariants clean` clause as `invariants clean, lint probe green|ran none`, or move the word into the sign-off summary) and extend dp3 (or lp1/lp2) to measure the success print of a probe-carrying fixture against INSTRUCTION_BYTES.

findings.issue: A shipped product script now executes any project file that happens to sit at `tools/prove-gates.py` at every sign-off, by filename convention alone, with no plan key opting in: a user project with an unrelated script at that path has it run with `--changed <paths>` and its exit 1 read as a not-proven stop and any other non-zero exit as a refusal that blocks sign-off. Every other gate the driver runs is named by the plan (meta.buildCommands, meta.runtimeBoot); this one is not. The executor flagged it as (b).
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): Key the probe off the plan (a `meta.buildCommands` entry or a dedicated meta key naming the probe command and declaring it speaks the `--changed` protocol), absent means skip; set it in this repo's plan. If that is out of this task's files, file it as a fix task before sign-off rather than shipping the filename convention.

findings.issue: Acceptance (4) is checked as equality of porcelain status letters + paths only. A file already dirty before the run (` M`) that the probe leaves mutated still reads ` M` after, so a stranded mutation in an already-modified lint file passes; conversely, a second session editing the shared checkout during the minutes-long run produces a false `left the checkout changed` stop whose remedy (`restore the tree`) would tell the operator to discard someone else's work.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): For entries dirty before the run, also compare a content digest (git hash-object of each) before and after; and word the stop as 'changed during the probe run' naming the entries without prescribing a restore, or refuse to start the probe when a path in the changed set is already dirty.

findings.issue: `subprocess.run` of a minutes-long mutating probe carries no timeout, so a hung probe hangs the sign-off step indefinitely with the tree possibly mid-mutation.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): Pass a timeout (a generous bound or one read from the plan), catch `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` as a refusal stop; the status comparison in `finally` already reports what a killed run left.

findings.issue: lp6's 'at another HEAD it runs once' twin calls `lint_probe(..., None)`, which short-circuits the hold on `if head and ...`; it never exercises a different SHA, so a hold that ignored the head comparison (e.g. `held.get("head")` truthy) would still pass lp6.
findings.resolution: fixed in P142.12-6yq (e236bb23ae07): Call the twin with a different 40-hex head (`"b" * 40`) so the comparison itself is what lets it run.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'Split each into staged blocks so the sweep spreads them across workers, and re-record the cost table.' The table is untouched, so the four split files keep the figures they had when each ran unsplit on one slot. Those figures now set the shard balance and every split file's timeout. On the live table, shard 3/3 holds three staged suites in a row (test_close_phase 330.3, test__deps 268.2, test_stamp_verification 265.4). The per-block process overhead on Windows, where test_stamp_verification now starts a process for each of its blocks, has never been measured. Once this lands on a CI run, save each Windows selftests cell's log and run `python tools/sweep-selftests.py --costs-from-log <logs> --platform windows-latest --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json`. findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'Acceptance: (1) time python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py is under 240 s wall on this machine twice, at least 20 minutes apart'. The executor measured 370.5 s and 370.9 s (20 min 11 s apart) and says itself that this is NOT MET. findings.issue: The diff makes three untouched documents state the old admission rule. CLAUDE.md says a staged suite 'is admitted with `stage_grant(jobs)` slots', CONTRIBUTING.md says 'is admitted holding `stage_grant(jobs)` slots', and the ci.yml comment says 'a staged suite is admitted holding all but one of them'. After slot_gate's change at tools/sweep-selftests.py:1385-1394, a suite holds as many slots as are free when its turn comes, between 1 and that number. The executor listed all three as stale and outside its files.
findings.resolution: Reword each to say: up to `stage_grant(jobs)` slots, as many as are free when its turn comes and at least one, with the number it holds passed to the child in SWEEP_STAGE_GRANT and its timeout calibrated to that number.

findings.issue: A staged suite's grant is fixed when it is admitted. If it is admitted with 1 slot, it runs every block serially (stage_workers=min(6,1)) for its whole run, even after other slots free up. Its timeout at held=1 is 3 x cost, which can exceed SWEEP_DEADLINE. tt5 still only bounds timeouts at the full grant, and its label was widened to accept that the deadline 'cuts ... a staged suite admitted late with fewer slots'. On today's windows table this is latent, not live. At jobs=4 the staged suite second in each shard gets 1 slot (shard 2/3: test_commit_task_work 222.9; shard 3/3: test__deps 268.2), and both serial costs are well under the 1380 s deadline. A rebalance that put test_audit_task (606.0) or test_drive_phase (1346.4) second in a shard would have the deadline cut a run that is slow, not hung, and nothing would turn red first.
findings.resolution: Add a tt5 sibling over the live table: for each `--shard i/3` at jobs=4, compute each staged suite's admitted slots (ticket order, with what is free at its turn, assuming earlier holders have not yet finished). Assert that file_timeout at those slots, and the serial cost it implies, stay under SWEEP_DEADLINE. That makes the latent case fail on the table change that creates it.

findings.file: tools/sweep-selftests.py:1761-1765 (one_block's timeout); cases tools/sweep-selftests.py:4007 bg6, :4306 tt0, :4321 tt1

findings.file: CLAUDE.md:239-243; CONTRIBUTING.md:330-334; .github/workflows/ci.yml:134-135; tools/sweep-selftests.py:1713 (sweep docstring), :1587-1590 (costs_from_rows docstring), :1604-1612 (record_costs 'about' text), :1474-1478 (shard comment)
findings.issue: These still describe the grant model the diff retired for every staged suite in the tree. CLAUDE.md says a staged_main suite 'is admitted with stage_grant(jobs) slots ... and is told the number in SWEEP_STAGE_GRANT, which sizes its block pool'. CONTRIBUTING.md and the ci.yml comment say the same. sweep()'s docstring says '`costs` orders the submissions (`run_order`)', but sweep() now orders by work_items. costs_from_rows, the shard comment and the record_costs 'about' string say the recorded figure is 'wall seconds times the slots ... the file held', but a block-run suite's figure is now the sum of its processes' seconds. The 'about' string is written into the committed .github/sweep-costs.json on the next --record-costs. The executor named the first three as followers, but no case and no task holds them.
findings.resolution: Rewrite each to the block model in this task or a follower task filed before sign-off: blocks are run as the sweep's jobs, one slot each, and replayed via --replay; a suite whose STAGES is not a literal runs whole on a grant; a block-run suite's cost is the summed slot-seconds of its processes. Fix sweep()'s docstring to name work_items.

findings.issue: sh6 says 'a shard runs its costliest files FIRST, so the slowest suite starts at once', but it asserts run_order(), which sweep() no longer calls. Submission order is now work_items (:1743). bb3 pins work_items as a function, but no case shows that sweep() submits in that order. Reverting :1743 to any other order leaves sh6 and bb3 green. bb1 uses equal costs, so it cannot tell either.
findings.resolution: Retitle sh6 to what it asserts: the split's order. Add a case that sweeps, at jobs=1, a heavy plain file and a staged fixture whose per-block estimate is higher, with costs given, and reads the order off each row's windows (start times): costliest job first.

findings.issue: replayed() keeps the first entry for a label (by.setdefault) and drops any later one silently. A list naming one block twice - the shape a sweep that ran a block twice would hand over - replays one copy and is never named. The sweep cannot produce that today: labels are unique by stage_labels, paths are set-deduped, and there is one counter per suite. But the replay is meant to be the honest reading, and it names a missing block and a stray block yet not a doubled one.
findings.resolution: Count labels in entries. A label listed more than once becomes one failing case '<label> RAN TWICE'. Add it to sr15's list, red-first by restoring setdefault.

findings.issue: The clause 'at some moment blocks of both run' rests on a-blocks sleeping 0.3 s, measured inside each child after its own interpreter start. It fails whenever b1's sleep starts more than 0.3 s after the last a-block's sleep began. That is start-up jitter, which the executor itself measured at load average 18-20 on 10 cores, and this case runs inside a full sweep's 8 workers. The other clauses (two b blocks at once, never more than four) are robust.
findings.resolution: Lengthen the a nap (for example 1.5 s, still well under b's 3 s), or read concurrency off the rows' per-process windows that sweep() now returns, rather than off in-sleep spans.

findings.issue: RUNNER_LINE_END_PENDING leaves the class open in _runner_output._pytest_cases/_pytest_tally and stamp-verification.final_error, and its comment explains the rows by a task boundary ("files the change that added this lint did not own"), which stops being true the moment another task touches them. The rows have no owner recorded where the next reader will look, and the docstring's own advice (a function handed normalised text should call plain_text itself, since it is idempotent) is not applied to these sites. runner_line_end_violations(pending=()) on the real tree returns exactly these three sites (_runner_output.py:444, :594, stamp-verification.py:728), so the debt is real and measured.
findings.resolution: State the reason in terms of the code (the public caller normalises; final_error strips after matching), not the change that added the lint, and file or name the follow-up task that deletes each row (calling plain_text inside the three functions costs nothing and removes them).

findings.issue: The house_red fixture is built with odd string surgery ("SELFTEST FAILED: 2/3 cases " + "passed\n" and "1/2 files ok, %d cases\n" % (5,)), which reads as a contrivance to get past the prose-number lint and makes the fixture harder to read than the output it imitates.

findings.issue: The committed cost table's `about` text still reads 'wall seconds times the slots of the sweep's budget the file held' - the very sentence the task's second med clause lists as false ('record_costs about text ... which --record-costs writes into .github/sweep-costs.json'). The diff corrects the generator (record_costs, tools/sweep-selftests.py) but not the file it wrote, so the repo now carries the retired-model wording until someone re-records. The executor disclosed this and says it was told not to edit the file; nothing in the task description says so.
findings.resolution: Replace the `about` string in .github/sweep-costs.json with the text record_costs now writes (same bytes, no cost values touched), or file a follow-up that re-records the table and names it.

findings.issue: The new duplicate-label failure (replayed() third return value, replay_selftest 'RAN n TIMES') and its case sr18 live in tests/_harness.py, which the recorded gate (`python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/sweep-selftests.py`) does not select and tests.add does not name. Once the orchestrator sets lintProbe, /audit:phase add on a plan without a derived or excluding phaseGate writes `lintProbe` into each new phase's gate, so run-test-gate.py runs the mutating probe with no --changed (the whole probe, minutes, rewriting the tree) as an ordinary gate command. findings.resolution: Reword to say the recorded gate run is held to it, or pass the bound to derive-phase-gate.py if it takes one.

tasks.title: Red-first through a sweep-shaped command proves when the task's suites pass and its new cases were red at HEAD
tasks.description: Reproduce on the filed P131.11 case (stamp-verification.py red --project <tree> --task P131.11 -- python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/release.py tools/check-example-pins.py) and find which reader rejects the fix-side output, which today reads 'the task's tests do not all pass (no tally or error reader matched its output)' while the same command exits 0 in the task tree. The cause is not established: the candidates are the fix-side run's environment (the sweep's isolation inside the helper's throwaway), the per-file versus summary reader, and the time budget. So a row's "output", and every line the sweep itself parses, reads "\n" on every platform.
2. A case that fails on today's code on any platform: a fixture child that writes "\r\n" line ends as raw bytes, run through the sweep. Its row output and the replay count read the same as a "\n" child's. Red-first it on posix by writing the CRLF bytes explicitly, so the case does not depend on the runner's platform.

tasks.title: Starting a task reads a repeated status row as a repeat, so a holder's duplicated block rows do not keep its own work charged
tasks.description:
Observed in P142 on 2026-10-27, on every restart of a single-dispatch task in the project checkout (three times in a row). `audit-task.py start` refused because another blocked task declares the same files. The release that exists for this case asks `_ran_within(_status_events(...))` whether the holder ran in the window, and it answered None ("cannot tell"). The cause is a real journal holding duplicate block rows: `in_progress->blocked` twice in the same second, then `None->blocked`. Both the drive and audit-task record the block, so the status chain reads as broken. Each time, the orchestrator had to set the work aside by hand, start, and restore it with sha256 checks.

Fix the reading, not the instance:
1. A status row whose `to` equals the state already reached is a repeat, not a break, whatever its `from` says (None included). Collapse repeats before the chain is judged.
2. Keep refusing a chain that is genuinely broken: a `from` that is neither the reached state nor None, or a row naming a different state with no transition into it.
3. Look at why two writers record the same block. If one of them is redundant, say so in your outcome; do not remove a journal writer in this task.

Red-first with the exact row shape copied from the real journal (same-second duplicate plus a `None->blocked`). It must read as "did not run within the window" where that is true. Add an over-fire case: a genuinely broken chain still answers None, and the refusal still fires. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

add: tests/test_audit_task.py: a journal holding a same-second duplicate block row and a None-to-blocked row reads as one transition, and a genuinely broken chain still answers cannot-tell

outcome.technical: Added _status_chain(events) in plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py: folds a row whose `to` equals the reached state into the row that reached it when its `from` is None, the reached state, or the `from` of the row that reached it; returns None when a move-on row does not start at the reached state, or a repeat names any other from. _ran_within now judges that chain instead of the raw adjacent-pair check; its last-event-vs-current check is unchanged. _status_events and _filed_while_running untouched. Tests (tests/test_audit_task.py, after hw11): hw13 real-shaped rows (manifest.edit pending->in_progress, task.block, manifest.edit and task.blocked all in_progress->blocked in the same second, wave.done None->blocked) -> window after block answers False, window straddling the run answers True; hw14 four genuinely broken chains (repeat with a stale other from, None->different state, from a never-reached state, last change not ending at current) all answer None. Mutation: repeat accepting any from -> hw14 red; fix absent -> hw13 red. Gate: sweep of tests/test_audit_task.py 1127 cases ok; tests/test__deps.py 254 ok; tests/test__output_lints.py 173 ok. Run bare (outside the sweep's isolation) lo-po4 fails because the suite warns it stands in a checkout; it passes under the sweep. Interpretation note: the task's rule 1 says a repeat holds 'whatever its from says' and rule 2 refuses a from that is neither reached state nor None; the real journal's repeat carries the previous state as its from (in_progress->blocked twice), so I accept None, the reached state, or the reaching row's own from as a repeat, and keep refusing any other from. Redundant writer: for one block three rows are written - the CLI's task.block (via cli), the hook's manifest.edit (via hook, same changes entry, no extra information) and the hook's task.blocked (carries attempt number, unique). The manifest.edit hook row duplicates the CLI row's status change and is the redundant one; no writer was removed.
outcome.descriptive: A holder's duplicated block rows no longer make the journal unreadable, so the start can tell a blocked holder did not run in the window instead of keeping its work charged.

tasks.title: The red-first helper sizes its deadline from the command's recorded cost and reads a stage missing at base as red
tasks.description:
Observed in P142 on 2026-10-27. P142.20-6yq's submit ran the red-first helper on `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py tests/test__worktrees.py` with the default 480 s deadline, half of it held back for the fix run. test_drive_phase records about 1349 slot-seconds in .github/sweep-costs.json. The base run therefore timed out and the return was filed `could-not-prove`. Narrowing to the task's new stage cannot help: HEAD's test file has no such stage, so the base run refuses with `unknown_stage_label`. Every tdd task gated on the drive suite loses mechanical red-first.

Fix the structure:
1. The deadline is sized from the command it is handed. When the command is a sweep, read the recorded costs of the files it names from the sweep's own cost table (reuse the sweep's reader; do not parse the JSON a second time), scaled by the same per-cost factor the sweep uses for a file's timeout. Keep `--timeout` as an explicit override. When no cost is recorded, keep today's default and say so in the basis.
2. A stage the fix run has and HEAD's file lacks is not a refusal. It means those cases did not exist at base, which is red for those cases. Say exactly that in the basis.
3. The basis text names the deadline it used and where the deadline came from.

Red-first: a fixture sweep command whose recorded cost exceeds the default, which times out today and completes after the fix. A stage missing at base, which refuses today and reads red after the fix. Add an over-fire case: an unrecorded command keeps the default deadline. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: A build command that runs at sign-off is never defaulted into a phase's gate
tasks.description:
Review finding P142-R22 (med), on P142.12-6yq at its landing. The sign-off lint probe is now named by `meta.buildCommands.lintProbe` (drive-phase.py `LINT_PROBE_KEY`). But `_manifest_phases.phase_gate_default()` defaults a new phase's gate to every `buildCommands` key that `meta.phaseGate.exclude` does not name. The only keys it skips are the review-only ones (`_manifest_vocab.review_only_keys`: the `REVIEW_ONLY_GATES` catalog, plus values starting `review-only:`). So once a plan sets `lintProbe`, `/audit:phase add` on a plan with no excluding `phaseGate` writes `lintProbe` into each new phase's gate. Then run-test-gate runs a probe that mutates the tree, as an ordinary gate step, on every task and phase gate.

Fix the vocabulary, not the one key:
1. A `buildCommands` key can be a sign-off step rather than a gate command. Give the catalog that category beside the review-only one (`lintProbe` is its first member), in `_manifest_vocab`, and make it the one place both questions are answered.
2. `phase_gate_default` skips sign-off-only keys exactly as it skips review-only keys, and its basis names what it skipped.
3. A phase or task gate that names a sign-off-only key explicitly is reported by the plan's validation (validate-manifest), with a message that says the key runs at sign-off and not as a gate step. Find where `_check_phase_gate` warns about an always/exclude overlap and put the check beside it.
4. Any other reader that builds a gate from `buildCommands` keys (grep `buildCommands` for derivations) reads the same predicate.

Red-first each case:
- a plan with `lintProbe` set and no `phaseGate` defaults a new phase's gate without it (red today);
- an explicit gate entry naming it is reported;
- over-fire: an ordinary key is still in the default, and a review-only key is still skipped.
No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

outcome.technical: _manifest_vocab: new LINT_PROBE_KEY, SIGNOFF_ONLY_GATES=(LINT_PROBE_KEY,), signoff_only_entry(entry), signoff_only_keys(build), beside the review-only catalog. _manifest_phases: re-exports them (LINT_PROBE_KEY, SIGNOFF_ONLY_KEYS, signoff_only_entry, signoff_only_keys); phase_gate_default skips sign-off-only keys from entries and from always, returns them as signoffOnly and names them in basis; new _signoff_only_gate (code phases.signoff_only_gate.in-gate) called from _check_phase_gate (meta.phaseGate.always only; exclude naming it stays quiet), _check_phase_intent (phase testGate) and _walk_phases (non-terminal task tests.gate). drive-phase.py: LINT_PROBE_KEY = _phases.LINT_PROBE_KEY (import layers allow it: drive-phase already imports _manifest_phases; no new import).
